guard_streams.source: Evaluation of BDUK Gigabit Vouchers: Initial Impacts and Benefits
guard_streams.write_limit: Historic voucher counterfactuals and beneficiary surveys are programme evaluation evidence, not current parcel coverage or measured performance.

facts.detail: The initial-impact evaluation was published on 30 August 2022.
GOV.UK classifies the publication as research and analysis.
The publication lists DSIT, BDUK and DCMS as responsible bodies.
The linked technical publication is a 126-page report.
The evaluation covers GBVS and Rural Gigabit Connectivity vouchers.
Hatch, Belmana and Winning Moves were appointed to conduct the evaluation.
The report examines effects on broadband availability and performance.
Counterfactual analysis covers vouchers issued in 2019 and 2020.
The report analyses a small-business beneficiary survey conducted in early 2022.
The publication is one report in the wider BDUK voucher-evaluation series.

guard_streams.source: GigaHubs Process Review Theory of Change
guard_streams.write_limit: Programme theory, eligibility and historic site counts do not establish current service availability or measured speed for surrounding private parcels.

facts.detail: The theory centres on eligible public buildings such as GP surgeries, libraries and schools.
Expected impacts include improved services, new services and reduced process time and resources.
The theory was revised from the 2025 evaluation plan using 2026 process-review findings.
The model links programme inputs to outputs, outcomes and impacts.
£110 million of Project Gigabit's £5 billion allocation was made available for Hubs.
The product was expected to complete in 2026 with no further funding beyond 2025/26.
BDUK funding covered capital elements of connectivity upgrades.
Supplier OMR data made public-site eligibility time-sensitive.
Rapid commercial rollout reduced eligible sites from 4,603 to 1,207 between 2020 and 2022.
Estimated viable Tier 1 local authorities fell from 30-60 to 10-20 after other school-connectivity routes were considered.
